title: fix(spec,objectql)!: a permission set's body packageId that disagrees with the package shipping it is refused at the build and registration doors; both readers read the binding only
body:
Fixes #23312
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

## What this does

The seat ruling on #23259, carried to the doors PR #23311 did not reach: a permission set's body `packageId` must agree with its package binding, or it is refused with a prescription (ADR-0086 D3: "the owning package for a package-shipped set (absent ⇒ env-authored)").

- **One judge.** The comparison and its words move out of `metadata-protocol` (where `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` was module-private) into `@objectstack/spec/security` as `judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding` (new file `packages/spec/src/security/permission-set-owner-binding.ts`). It returns data (`declared`, `bound`, `message`, `issueMessage`); each door builds its own envelope. It gains two doors, `build` and `register`. `protocol.ts` keeps its wrapper and its name (so its `{@link}`s stand); the edit there is that function's body, its docblock and the `@objectstack/spec/security` import line. The save, restore and publish words are byte-identical (measured below).
- **The build door.** A refinement on `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate`, beside `applyApiEndpointGates`, whose docblock gives the reason to put it on the schema: `defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`, the lint scorer and the artifact door all run this one parse). Bindings: no `packages[]`, every top-level set against `manifest.id` (no manifest means no package); with `packages[]`, each body's sets against that body's `id`, and a top-level set no body declares (the residual) against `manifest.id`. A top-level set that a body declares is that body's copy, which is never registered from the top level, so it is not judged at the top level. `defineStack` answers `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` / 422 with the issue at `permissions.N.packageId`. No code minted.
- **The registration door.** `ObjectQL.registerMetadataCollections` (manifest and nested plugin) throws `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 (`httpStatus` 400, `issues[]` at `packageId`) before `registerItem` files the set. **Sibling matched:** `viewContainerNameRefusal`, the same loop's other body-against-key refusal, thrown one statement earlier in the same envelope. It covers the manifests no schema parse judged: a programmatic `registerApp`, a nested plugin, a `strict: false` stack, a package from a stored manifest.
- **Both readers read the binding only.** `plugin-security` `declaredPackageIdOf`: one line, `item._packageId ?? item.packageId` becomes `item._packageId` (epic #15194's territory is not otherwise touched). `cli` `collectPermissionSetDeclarations`: `manifestId ?? asId(ps.packageId)` becomes `manifestId`, and its docblock stops describing the fallback as the rule.
- `PermissionSetSchema.packageId` describe and TSDoc name every door (`content/docs/references/security/permission.mdx` regenerated). The step-18 entry `permission-set-package-id-binding-mismatch-refused` is widened to the build and registration doors; its old sentence "Package source (defineStack permissions) is not judged by this entry" is replaced.

## Zone 2, measured

- **H1 holds.** `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` was module-private (`protocol.ts:994` at `6d96721fa`), and `packages/spec` cannot import `metadata-protocol`. The diff adds a published export: `api-surface/security.json` gains `judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding` (function), `PermissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` (interface) and `PermissionSetOwnerBindingDoor` (type). No error code is added. So `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` stands as claimed.
- **H2 holds, and more widely than stated.** `os validate` runs the same `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` (`validate.ts:349`), so one refinement serves both doors. Measured through the real CLI (`bin/run.js validate --json`, built `dist`) on three scratch projects:
  - strict `defineStack` with `packageId: 'com.probe.other'` under manifest `com.probe.pkg`: exit 1, `code: STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`, `✗ permissions.0.packageId: Drop packageId from permission set 'probe_member', or ship the set from package 'com.probe.other' …` (the refusal raised by the config's own `defineStack` at load);
  - the same with `{ strict: false }`: exit 1, `valid: false`, `errors[0]` = `custom` at `permissions.0.packageId` (os validate's own parse);
  - the key equal to the manifest id: exit 0, `valid: true`.
  The no-manifest stack: ADR-0086 D3 with PR #23311's rule for a set saved into no package settles it. A stack with no manifest registers its sets into no package (measured: `registerApp` with no id files the set with no `_packageId`), so a present key, the empty string included, is refused. No fork to decide. (`AppPlugin` already refuses to boot such a stack: an app payload with no id throws at construction.)
- **H3 holds.** Re-measured on `6d96721fa` before any edit, with the built `ObjectQL`. A manifest `com.probe.pkg` whose set declares `packageId: 'com.probe.other'` registers as `{"_packageId":"com.probe.pkg","packageId":"com.probe.other","_provenance":"package"}`, and a nested plugin does the same. Zero `console.warn` or `console.error` lines are captured. A manifest with no id registers `{"packageId":"com.probe.other"}` with no `_packageId` at all, which is the one shape where the lock reader's fallback named the body key as the owner. After the change, all three are refused with `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400 and nothing is filed. An equal key and an absent key register under `com.probe.pkg` as before.
- **H4 holds.** Lock reader: `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts:178` read `item._packageId ?? item.packageId`. A registry item (or code-layer envelope) with no binding and a body key was classified `packaged` under the body's package. It now reads `org`. Cli reader: `permission-set-name-collisions.ts:157` read `manifestId ?? asId(ps.packageId)`. With no manifest id the collision check now reads no owner, so the declaration is dropped as unowned: the retired seeder's `if (!packageId)` arm, never a collision. Pinned. Two sets of one name naming two different packages in their bodies used to be reported as a cross-package collision; now they are not.
- **H5: the gate does not ask for widening.** `check-adr-0087-registration` accepts `not-required (already-registered permission-set-package-id-binding-mismatch-refused)`, because the id predates the merge base. It can only verify that the id resolves, not that the entry covers the change, so the entry is widened in this diff to keep that claim true. The gate's verdict: `1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition … not-required (already-registered)`.

## Pins, each with a negative control, and the ablations

| pin | file | control |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the judge's verdict table at all five doors; build and register words prescribe first | `spec/src/security/permission-set-owner-binding.test.ts` | equal and absent keys accepted at every door |
| `defineStack` refuses (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`/422, issue `custom` at `permissions.0.packageId`), no-manifest and `''` included, map format too; artifact bodies judged against their own id; residual judged against `manifest.id` | `spec/src/stack-permission-set-owner-binding.test.ts` | equal/absent accepted; a both-halves artifact's top-level copy NOT judged against the artifact id |
| `registerApp` refuses (`VALIDATION_ERROR`/400/`httpStatus` 400, `issues[]` at `packageId`), nested plugin and no-id manifest included, nothing filed | `objectql/src/permission-set-owner-registration.test.ts` | equal/absent register under the package |
| the lock never reads the body key (registry and code layer) | `plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts` | a binding decides, a disagreeing body key does not move it |
| the cli reader never reads the body key | `cli/src/utils/permission-set-name-collisions.test.ts` (the old "packageId answers only where no package ships the set" case is rewritten) | a manifest-bound stack declares every set under its manifest id |

Ablations were run on committed `9903d68d4`, through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (the anchor hit 1→0, the blob changed, and the tool restored and proved `blob == HEAD` and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Every subject is imported from `src` by a relative path, so no `dist` rebuild was involved. Each turned red in the expected direction, and its controls stayed green:

- build door (`.superRefine(applyPermissionSetOwnerBindingGate)` removed): `5 failed | 2 passed (7)`, the 2 being the controls;
- registration door (the refusal call replaced by `undefined`): `3 failed | 1 passed (4)`;
- lock reader (the `?? item.packageId` fallback restored): `2 failed | 25 passed (27)`;
- cli reader (the `?? asId(ps.packageId)` fallback restored): `1 failed | 10 passed (11)`.

**Byte-identity of the moved words.** `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal` was extracted from `git show 6d96721fa:packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, transpiled, and compared with `judgePermissionSetOwnerBinding` from the built `spec` dist. The comparison covered 180 cases (3 doors × 10 bodies × 6 bindings): 63 refusals and 0 differing in `message` or `issues[0].message`. PR #23311's door pins (`protocol.item-name-every-door.test.ts`) pass unchanged.

## Verification (local; CI runs the full farm)

Package suites, run under the verify lock at `9903d68d4` (pre-merge):

- `@objectstack/spec` (`--project local`): 672 files, 20434 passed, 1 todo.
- `@objectstack/objectql` (`--project local`): 414 files, 8070 passed.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: 228 of 238 files passed, 3 skipped, 28118 tests passed. 7 files failed to load with `Cannot find package '@objectstack/spec/api'`: a sibling gate rebuilt `spec/dist` mid-run, a resolution failure that never reached a test body. Re-run: those 7 files plus `protocol.item-name-every-door.test.ts`, 8 files, 264 passed.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security`: 189 files, 3881 passed, 45 skipped.
- `@objectstack/cli` (`--project unit`): 287 files, 4293 passed. The integration layer is declared to CI: the diff touches no integration-tier file and no spawn entry.

Typecheck: `typecheck` exits 0 for all five packages (`SPEC_TC=0 OQL_TC=0 MP_TC=0 PS_TC=0 CLI_TC=0`).

Generated artifacts: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` reports "All 14 generated artifacts are up to date" on the merged tree `14b1c5a25`, against a `spec` dist built from that tree. `api-surface`, `export-origins` and `docs` were regenerated by `--fix` (only the 3 it proved stale).

Gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths) derived 125 commands at `9903d68d4`, and all 125 ran. Reconciliation printed `--ran`: `125 derived, 125 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. Five of them first refused on prerequisites and were re-run green on the same tree:
- `check-engine-split-ratio` and the `check-plugin-teardown-shape` self-test, after `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-07-09`;
- `check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n-coverage`, once the unbuilt packages they read had `dist`.

`pnpm check:type-check-debt` was measured: `OK … 26 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number`. The PM's 86-command lead list is a subset of the 125 (the 39 extra are the changeset, docs and ratchet families the final diff touches).

**Named gap.** The gate union above was measured on `9903d68d4`. `origin/main` (`dc393266f`, which carries #23345's other-region edit to `protocol.ts`) was then merged as `14b1c5a25`, and the derived list there is identical (125, same commands). The post-merge re-run of the union and of the touched pins is in flight; its verdicts land in the `os-dev-report` comment on #23312.

Lint: `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 14 changed TS files gives 14 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Three facts make that narrowing a measurement:
- all 14 are inside the config's population (`files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}']` minus `NEVER_LINTED`);
- the count, 14, is read from the JSON output;
- `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting (its own note: "no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules"), so this diff cannot move a verdict on any untouched file.

Consumer sweep: `examples/**` holds 0 permission sets with a body `packageId` (the showcase's two `packageId` hits are capabilities). `turbo ls --affected` was not used to narrow anything: every consumer package named in the order was run in full. Its blind spot is stated anyway: it is built from the package graph, so it cannot see tests that read another package's source from disk.

## Acceptance notes

- **The environment-artifact door, by reading only.** `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata` embeds `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, so an environment artifact now refuses on a disagreeing set too. Its producer is the cloud control plane, and the schema calls the field "the direct output of `objectstack compile`": package source, which this ruling covers. Not measured here, because no cloud checkout is in this container.
- **Residual sets in `os validate`.** The top-level residual of a multi-package artifact is judged by the same schema rule. The "claimed" test for a permission set (a body declares a set of that name) mirrors `unclaimedTopLevel`'s slot rule in `@objectstack/metadata`. That rule cannot be imported into spec, so the docblock names it.
- `/tests-3pkg.pid` (6 bytes, a pid) was written at the filesystem root by a mistyped redirect in this session. Removing it was refused by the session's safety check, so it is left for a person. It is outside every repository.
